newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: New Russian bank ventures into Geneva.
newsitem.headline: New Russian bank ventures into Geneva.

text.p: A Russian regional bank, Rosestbank, has opened a representative office in Geneva, joining two other banks from Russia in Switzerland's private banking capital, Swiss media reported on Thursday.

Officials of the bank could not be reached for comment but French-language daily Tribune de Geneve quoted Swiss banking authorities as saying that the office had no right to conduct banking activities.

The bank, headquartered in the Russian town of Togliatti, home of the Lada car factory, was set up in 1992 and is a former affiliate of the Commercial Bank of Tartu in the Baltic republic of Estonia, the newspaper said.
It quoted the bank's vice-president in Geneva, Vadim Kebets, as saying the office would focus on contacts with institutional clients. "We will not accept money from unknown clients," he said.
Swiss authorities are worried by the flow of potentially-dirty money to Geneva from Russia where organised crime has soared since the Soviet collapse.
The two other Russian commercial banks operational in Geneva are Inkombank and Uneximbank.
